questions.def: "Flows" is intransitive; the river performs the action itself.
questions.question: The river ___ gently through the valley.

questions.def: "Placed" is transitive, requiring an object (the vase).
questions.question: She ___ the antique vase carefully on the table.

questions.def: "Walks" is used transitively here, requiring an object (dog).
questions.question: He ___ his dog in the park every evening.

questions.def: "Risen" (intransitive) describes the price's spontaneous increase.
questions.question: The price of oil has ___ significantly this year.

questions.def: "Increased" is transitive; the company acted on its profits.
questions.question: The company ___ its profits by 20% last quarter.

questions.def: "Laid" is transitive; use intransitive "lay" here.
questions.question: She laid down for a nap after lunch.

questions.def: "Seat" used transitively means to cause someone to sit.
questions.question: Please ___ yourself comfortably.

questions.def: "Lay" (intransitive, past tense) means to be in a resting position.
questions.question: The ship ___ in the harbor.

questions.def: "Laid" (transitive, past tense) means to place something down.
questions.question: He ___ the book on the shelf.

questions.def: "Hung" is the past tense of transitive "hang" (to suspend).
questions.question: He ___ the picture on the wall.

questions.def: "Hanged" (transitive) is used for execution by hanging.
questions.question: The criminal was ___ for his crimes.

questions.def: "Hung" (intransitive) means to be suspended.
questions.question: The flag ___ in the breeze.

questions.def: "Sat" is intransitive; use "set" (transitive) here.
questions.question: She sat the vase on the table.

questions.def: "Set" (transitive) means to arrange something on the table.
questions.question: Please ___ the table before dinner.

questions.def: "Rings" is intransitive; the alarm performs the action itself.
questions.question: The alarm ___ at 7 AM every morning.

questions.def: "Rang" (transitive) requires an object (the bell).
questions.question: He ___ the bell to summon the waiter.

questions.def: "Broke" is the past tense of the transitive verb "break."
questions.question: He ___ the vase accidentally.

questions.def: "Broke" is the past tense of the intransitive verb "break."
questions.question: The window ___ during the storm.

questions.def: "Chopped" is transitive, requiring an object (vegetables).
questions.question: The chef ___ the vegetables before cooking.

questions.def: "Opened" is the past tense of the transitive verb "open."
questions.question: He ___ the door for her.

questions.def: "Opened" is intransitive here, describing the door's action.
questions.question: The door ___ easily with a push.

questions.def: "Launched" is transitive, requiring an object (the product).
questions.question: The company ___ the new product last month.

questions.def: "Entered" is the past tense of the transitive verb "enter."
questions.question: He ___ the room quietly.

questions.def: "Entered" is used transitively here, implying active participation.
questions.question: She ___ the competition with confidence.

questions.def: "Flew" is intransitive; the bird performs the action itself.
questions.question: The bird ___ into the sky.

questions.def: "Gasp" is intransitive here, needing "at" to connect to the object.
questions.question: The audience gasped ___ the magician's unexpected disappearance.

questions.def: "Struck" is the correct past tense, used intransitively in this case.
questions.question: The antique clock ___ precisely at midnight.

questions.def: "Rising" is the present participle acting as an adjective.
questions.question: The ___ cost of living is a concern for many.

questions.def: "Lay" (transitive) requires a preposition to indicate location.
questions.question: He laid the book ___ the table carefully.

questions.def: "Flow" is the correct intransitive verb in this context.
questions.question: The river ___ through the valley.
